status: Passed at bffc599 on release binaries built from the committed source (state schema 18): 20 successive gated reloads of one private daemon, each predecessor retired within 14.0 s of the reload being asked for, while two agents printed numbered lines as fast as sh allows (6684278 lines, every log contiguous), a batch and a PTY fixture ran, CLI clients sent 900 numbered messages (all arrived once, in order, no errors) and launched 653 short agents, half stopped early (all reached a durable end, no send, launch or stop errors). A lease and a pending question kept their identity and expiry across every switch and the question was answered after the last. Covers the acceptance items: peer messages before and during transfer in order; log pressure; concurrent send, stop and launch; multiple successive replacements. Not covered here: provider receipts and active Claude or Codex conversations, replay retention limits, Windows.
scope: Acceptance before enabling reload in LIVE-DAEMON-UPGRADES.md, the parts a private daemon and CLI clients can establish without a provider account.
method: scripts/reload_acceptance.py --binary-dir target/release --reloads 20 (pause 0.3 s between reloads). The daemon is started with AGENTDOCKER_EXPERIMENTAL_RELOAD=1 and reloaded through `agentdocker daemon reload`, which waits through backpressure; every client goes through the CLI, so a transferring answer is retried the way every client retries it. The harness scans the chained daemon log for warnings and errors and records them under results.daemon_log_warnings.

scenarios: 900 messages sent through 20 reloads arrived once, in order; 0 send errors
653 agents launched (half stopped early) during the reloads all finished; 0 launch errors
both loggers' logs are contiguous across every reload
batch and PTY fixtures exit with exact codes under the last daemon with complete logs
a lease and a pending question kept their identity and expiry across every switch; the question was answered after the last

daemon_log_note: Every warning recorded is a fenced skip on an exit that landed during an offer: the predecessor keeps the owner's exit report rather than record it, the successor recovers it while still fenced and records it after acceptance; every launched agent reached a durable end, which the trial asserts. The longer reloads are `daemon reload` waiting through backpressure while launches or stops admitted before the offer finished.
path_redaction: Published account-home paths use <user-home>; recorded source and binary hashes are unchanged. Raw local records remain private.
